The game fundamentally revolves around constructing an independent set in the knight's graph of the $6 \times 6$ board. The maximum size of an independent set $\alpha(G)$ on a standard chessboard of size $N \times N$ (where $N$ is even) is $N^2/2$. For $6 \times 6$, $\alpha(G) = 36/2 = 18$.

Since Horst aims to maximize the size of this independent set $K$, and Queenie aims to minimize it by occupying key squares, the game is equivalent to who gets to claim the majority of the vertices in this maximum independent set (MIS).

**Optimal Strategies:**
1. **Horst's Strategy:** Horst always chooses an unoccupied square belonging to the largest color class (e.g., all white squares if the board is colored) that has not been attacked by previous knights. Since all squares in the MIS are mutually non-attacking, Horst can simply target any square in the MIS.
2. **Queenie's Strategy:** Queenie plays optimally to minimize $K$. Since the knights must form an independent set, Queenie's most effective strategy is to occupy squares that belong to the maximum independent set that Horst is targeting. She will always choose an unoccupied square from the MIS.
